- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially near end of horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots in early days of forecast horizon (e.g., day 1–3) when sentiment is volatile; apply downward bias to first 3 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.67) triggers model lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- Horizon-specific: last 3–5 days of forecast often overcorrect; apply mild downward adjustment (0.5–1.5%) to avoid overfitting to recent sentiment.
